RMP Executive Summary

1.	Facility Policy.  KAAPA Ethanol, L.L.C corporate policies place the utmost importance on workers, public, and environmental safety, which is reflected in facility plans and training activities.  The owners, management and employees of the KAAPA Ethanol facility are committed to the prevention of any accidental releases of hazardous materials.  If an accidental release should occur, the facility is prepared to work with the local fire department, Kearney County Emergency Management (Local Emergency Planning Committee), and/or other authorities, to mitigate and minimize the impacts of the release to the public and the environment.

2.	Facility Information. The primary activity at the facility is the processing of grain into fuel-grade ethyl alcohol.  The ethyl alcohol manufacturing process involves the use of anhydrous ammonia and natural gasoline.  The natural gasoline is referred to as product denaturant and is used to make the ethyl alcohol unfit for human consumption.      

3.	Five-Year Accident History.  A release of CorrPRO 656T in the tank farm.  Release caused by the wrong valve being opened.  NDEE 052622-RS-1200.

4.	Emergency Response.  The emergency response program established by KAAPA Ethanol allows personnel to respond to accidental releases of regulated substances in the event the release can be controlled using KAAPA Ethanol personnel and equipment in the area.  KAAPA Ethanol has identified additional resources to assist in mitigation, control and disposal of release.  The local emergency response agencies will be relied upon to inform the public about the release. KAAPA Ethanol has developed an Emergency Action Plan outlining actions taken in the event of an accidental release of regulated substances as well as in the event of natural disasters.  The Emergency Action Plan is provided below for reference.  

5.	KAAPA Ethanol has an Emergency Response Action Plan (ERAP) in place to respond to prevent and respond to chemical sp

ills on site. The details in the ERAP are provided after the Emergency Action Plan within this Executive Summary. 

6.	Accidental Release Prevention Program.   KAAPA Ethanol, L.L.C. plant has implemented several environmental, emergency, and safety programs at the facility.  These plans are crucial in our everyday operation and procedures.  Daily, weekly, and monthly checks are completed that affect our ability to respond to emergencies, including a Health and Safety Plan.   Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) and Storm Water Pollution Prevention (SWPP) plans have been prepared and implemented, with updates completed as needed to ensure compliance and effectiveness.   All implementation is accordance with the applicable regulatory standards and time frames.  KAAPA Ethanol has developed a Prevention Program in accordance with the requirements of 40 CFR Part 68 for a Program Level 3 facility.  The facility conducts weekly and monthly training as part of our normal activities.  Training consists of regulated safety requirements.  A Process Safety Management (PSM) program has been implemented in accordance to regulation.  Natural gasoline (denaturant) is a PSM-applicable chemical mixture on site.  The PSM program covers distillation tanks and piping, and storage tanks utilized for anhydrous ethanol and denatured ethyl alcohol.   Safety inspections are completed regularly, utilizing in-house and outside expertise to conduct.  Periodic reviews are completed on plans and procedures in place, with scheduling for additional training as part of the review process.  As previously mentioned in section 5 of this executive summary, KAAPA Ethanol implements an ERAP as part of the Spill Prevention Control & Countermeasure requirement to prevent and respond to chemical spills on site. In addition, KAAPA Ethanol has a Facility Response Plan (FRP) to respond to chemical spills on site. Both the ERAP and the FRP are regulated under the Oil Pollution Prevention regulatio

n.
A preventative system (Llumin CMMS system) is used by KAAPA Ethanol to confirm chemical storage tanks are in proper working condition.

7.	Planned changes to Improve Safety.  Safety improvements are an on-going process at KAAPA Ethanol.  Periodic evaluations are performed to assess the conditions of the facility.  KAAPA Ethanol has a metal integrity written plan in place to confirm chemical storage tanks are in proper working condition. A preventative system (Lumin) is also used by KAAPA Ethanol to confirm chemical storage tanks are in proper working condition.  KAAPA also uses PROTect, an outside firm to track MI inspections and findings.

EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN 

I)	Policy Statement: KAAPA Ethanol, LLC believes that its employees are its most important asset, and that their safety and health are among its greatest responsibilities.  Therefore, this Emergency Action Plan has been established in compliance with the OSHA standard, Title 29 CFR 1910.38(a), and posted for all employees.

II)	Purpose: This Emergency Action Plan is intended to ensure the proper response to foreseeable emergencies and where necessary ensure the orderly evacuation of employees from work locations to a safe area away from conditions that could be immediately dangerous to life and health.  

III)	Responsibility and Authority
A.	Program Coordinator=Assigned to Safety and Environmental Manager to oversee:
 1.	The development, implementation, and ongoing improvement of this Emergency Action Plan.
 2.	Development and posting of the Emergency Action Plan and site exit diagram.
 3.	All emergency equipment is inspected at various intervals to ensure proper operation of all emergency equipment.
 4.	Periodic drills of the emergency action plan.

   B)		Visitors=Visitors, Contractors, Vendors, Non-employees entering the facility

2.	Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.  4:30 p.m. all visitors will sign in and out at the administrative office.  In the event the

work schedule starts or continues past normal office hours sign in will be completed at control room check/sign in ledger.
3.	Monday  Friday between 4:30 p.m.  7:30 a.m. all visitor/contractors will check/sign  in and out at the control room ledger. Contractors on site are required to always supply information including company name and total number of personnel on site.
4.	Contractors, if not accompanied by a KAAPA employee may be given a radio to communicate critical or emergency situations in the event one arises.  This will be determined during project planning, pre-job briefing, or heightened security risk.  
5.	If an evacuation is required, the control room board operator will collect check/sign in ledger, located in control room as a means of identifying contractors on site.  The administrative office will collect check in cards/ledger and gather at the safe gathering location.  A role call will occur, in the event someone is presumed to be missing, attempts will be made through radio communication.  If unsuccessful wait for emergency services to arrive before reentering the facility.

Definitions:
Term	Definition
Plant Emergency	Any undesired event that could lead to the personal injury of employees, contractors, or visitors, or the damage to KAAPA Ethanol, LLC property.
Active Shooter	An individual who is engaged in killing or attempting to kill people in a confined and populated area; in most cases, active shooters use firearms and there is no pattern or method to their selection of victims.
Gas Shut Off or Significant Change in Gas Flow	Means that if a plant upset, or any abnormal disturbance to natural gas flow to the facility is made, either planned or as part of an emergency shutdown. See Energy Maintenance Services provisions.
Severe Weather Watch	Means that conditions are favorable for development of a severe storm.  This may include such things as high winds, heavy rain, hail and/or lightning.  The winter version, Severe Winter Storm Warning, could also produce heavy snow, and hazardous sub-zero wind chills.
Severe Weather Warning	Indicates that a dangerous storm is imminent.  Note:  A severe weather warning is not necessarily a prerequisite step for a tornado warning.  When conditions are favorable for severe weather, they may also be favorable for a tornado.  It is possible for a severe weather warning and tornado conditions to be present at the same time.
Tornado Watch	Issued by the National Weather Ser

vice, indicates the weather conditions are adequate for the development of a tornado. A watch condition could exist for up to 12 hours.
Tornado Warning	Means a tornado or funnel cloud has been sighted in the area, or is indicated on radar.  Tornado warning status means there is immediate danger of tornado(s), and that tornado emergency procedures should be initiated.

2.	Tornado  In the event of a tornado warning all plant personnel are to take shelter in the grain pits, restrooms, or shelter in maintenance building.  Administrative personnel are to take shelter in the basement restrooms of the administrative office building.  Contractors and all drivers onsite during a tornado warning will be required to take shelter in the grain receiving pit or restroom areas.

X)	Action plans for potential emergencies
1.	Fire evacuation procedures
?	If a fire is discovered in its incipient (initial, early) stage:

2.	If the fire has spread or appears to be to big for ONE extinguisher to handle, or the area is thick with smoke:
?	Sound the alarm activating the fire alarm system
?	Notify Crew Chief, Call emergency services 911 
?	Determine if Evacuation is Needed, Evacuate to the Parking Lot on the Northeast Side of the Administrative Building 
?	At the Parking Lot on the Northeast Side of the Administrative Building inform the Incident Manager exactly why you called for the evacuation and whether emergency services were contacts.
3.	All employees will, upon hearing the alarm, evacuate to the Parking Lot on the  North East Side of the Administrative Building (see diagram)
4.	Evacuation Wardens will, upon hearing the alarm:
?	Ensure their areas are evacuated, telling people along the way where to gather.

?	Report to the Incident Manager at the Parking Lot on the East Side of the Administrative Building.
5.	The incident manager will:
?	Ensure emergency services are contacted.
?	If Natural Gas to the plant needs to be shut off, Identify and designate an employee to close either the valve behind the Energy Center or our main station behind the Cooling Tower.
?	Communicate and coordinate with emergency services upon their arrival.
?	Notify the Environmental Health & Safety Manager.
?	Account for Personnel
6.	The incident manager will:
?	Announce the all clear, or
?	Determine when it is safe to return to work.

B)	?	Tornado Procedures:
1.	During a Tornado warning, personnel will be informed of the hazard via radio.  
2.	Employees will take shelter in Grain Silo Pits, Break Room Restroom, Records Room in Maintenance building, or Basement Restrooms of Administrative Building, 
3.	The Evacuation Wardens will, upon hearing the notification, ensure their areas are evacuated, telling people along the way where to take shelter.
4.	If time does not permit taking shelter in the designated areas, employees should:

E)	Active Shooter Event:

?	Active shooter procedures and hot to respond when an active shooter is in your vicinity determine the most reasonable way to protect your own life. Remember that customers and clients are likely to follow the lead of employees and managers during an active shooter situation.
	RUN (If there is an accessible escape path, attempt to evacuate the premises. Be sure to:
	Have an escape route and plan in mind.
	Evacuate regardless of whether others agree to follow.
	Leave your belongings behind
	Help others escape if possible.
	Prevent individuals from entering an area where the active shooter may be 
	Keep your hands visible.
	Follow the instructions of any police officers.
	Do not attempt to mov

e wounded people.
	Call 911 when you are safe.
	HIDE (if the evacuation is not possible, find a place to hide where the active shooter is less likely to find you. Your hiding place should
?	Be out of the active shooters view.
?	Provide protection if shots are fired in your direction (i.e. an office with a closed and locked door)
?	Not to trap you or restrict your options for movement.
	To prevent an active shooter from entering your hiding place:
?	Lock the door.
?	Block the door with heavy furniture
	If the active shooter is nearby:
?	Lock the door.
?	Silence your cell phone and/or pager
?	Turn off any source of noise (i.e., radios, televisions_
?	Hide behind large items (i.e., cabinets, desks)
?	Remain quiet.
	If evacuation and hiding out are not possible:
?	Remain calm.
?	Dial 911, if possible, to alert police to the active shooters location
?	If you cannot speak, leave the line open and allow the dispatcher to listen.
	FIGHT-As a last resort, and only when your life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt and/or incapacitate the active shooter by:
?	Acting as aggressively as possible against him/her
?	Throwing items and improvising weapons
?	Yelling
?	Committing to your actions.
